subject: Model entry checklist and fallback policy for Argus-7B-v2
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-05T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Model entry checklist + fallback policy for Argus-7B-v2

Hi team,

Aurelius (contact: Sara Lin) has submitted Argus-7B-v2 for onboarding to our hosted catalog and is asking to pin the variant for their Dedicated staging cluster while they validate outputs. They want a short path to prod if checks pass.

High level asks: 
- Run compatibility checklist (weights/layout, KV cache format, tokenization edge cases). I attached their model spec and our onboarding checklist.
- Confirm quantization path (int4/int8) and any accuracy regressions we should surface to the customer.
- Provide a conservative pin/fallback recommendation (e.g., pin to argus-7b-v2 + automatic fallback to argus-7b-v1-lite or open-llm-generic-7b).
- Proposed rollout: canary at 5-10% for 48 hours with latency and quality regression alerts.

Laura/Dev: can you scope runtime perf and compatibility runs? Neha: can you run a quick privacy/risk surface review for the new tokenizer changes noted in the spec? I cc'd Vanessa to coordinate the timeline and external comms.

Attachments:
- model_spec_argus_v2.pdf (external vendor spec)
- compatibility_checklist.xlsx (onboarding checklist)

Goal: have a go/no-go recommendation and rollout plan by EOD Friday so we can schedule the customer briefing next week.

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Product Manager, Model Ops
Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-05T11:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Model entry checklist + fallback policy for Argus-7B-v2

Thanks Hannah — quick update from the runtime side after an initial probe against the sample weights: 

- KV cache format: Argus v2 changed the KV packing for multihead attention (additional stride introduced). This will break our existing hot-path unless we add a lightweight adapter during compilation.
- Attention kernel: on A100 our 32-bit attention kernel falls back to a slower generic path for some sequence lengths in the vendor tarball. Need to reproduce on our microbench harness.
- Tokenizer: there are ~80 OOV tokens compared to our tokenization baseline; we should include a small eval that checks perplexity and token-level edits.

Action items I can take: 
1) Run compatibility harness across our kernel matrix (A100, H100, T4) — ETA 48-72 hours. I will log results to SUP-2248.
2) Produce a short compatibility report (compat_report_draft.txt) with recommended adaptation steps (adapter for KV layout + quantization checklist).

Operational ask: please confirm if pinning to v2 should be executable immediately on Dedicated staging clusters only (recommended) and that we configure automatic fallback to a v1-compatible variant. I recommend a conservative canary (10%) as Hannah suggested; we need the customer aware of possible 2-3% tail latency increases during initial roll.

I attached the draft compat report and linked the Jira.

— Dev
Dev Patel
Infrastructure Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-05T14:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Model entry checklist + fallback policy for Argus-7B-v2

Putting in my estimate:
- Perf & stability runs across our standard scenarios: 3 business days (includes quantized int4/int8 pass).
- Integration test for prefix/KV caching behavior + regression monitors: additional 2 business days.

I can prioritize the A100/H100 runs first and hand off the T4 queue after. To run the evals I need: the curated prompt set (small eval subset) and the vendor's validation slices. Sara/Sales: can you provide the eval prompts or give permission to use our redwood-internal dev set?

Fallback suggestion: implement rollout policy that pins traffic to argus-7b-v2 on a per-customer routing rule with an automatic switch to argus-7b-v1-lite on any of the following thresholds: 
- 95th latency > baseline + 125ms for > 10 minutes
- Quality drift > 3 metric points on the prompt set for 30m
- Error rate spike > 0.5%

I've attached a small runtime estimate CSV with provisional token-cost delta.

Laura Bennett
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lin <sara@aurelius.ai>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-05T17:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Model entry checklist + fallback policy for Argus-7B-v2

Hi Sara — looping you in with the internal team so we can align on a safe onboarding plan for Argus-7B-v2. Summary of internal plan: 

- Redwood will run compatibility + perf checks (Dev/Laura) and surface a go/no-go by Friday EOD.
- If we proceed, we will pin v2 to a Dedicated staging cluster for Aurelius with a 10% canary and automatic fallback rules as suggested by Laura.
- Neha will complete a short privacy/risk note on tokenizer changes.

Requested from Aurelius: the validation prompt set or permission to run Redwood dev prompts against the model (this shortens our ETA). Also confirm if the vendor requires any special handling of logs or data retention.

Next step: 30-minute sync tomorrow 9:30am PT to review the initial compatibility findings (invite incoming). If that time doesn't work, propose alternatives.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference
